QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_25

question.text: Mr. Dhruv Menon, IR head at Sindhu Opportunities Fund, is designing the standard quarterly LP report. Which of the following sets of line-items BEST matches the contents that Indian Cat II AIFs typically include in fund reporting and benchmarking?

answer.text: Trustee meeting minutes, IC decisions, GP travel expenses, director remuneration
Clearing-member margin usage, VaR, derivative exposure, daily P&L
SEBI activity return, KRA/CKYC status, AML red flags, STR filings
Portfolio snapshot and allocation, deals and exits, valuation/performance reporting, and DPI/RVPI/TVPI benchmarking multiples

explanation.text: The Logic: Fund-level reports and benchmarking for Indian Cat II AIFs typically cover the current portfolio snapshot and allocation, deals done and exits, portfolio-company developments, and valuation/performance reporting. Benchmarking uses standard private-market multiples such as DPI (distributions to paid-in), RVPI (residual value to paid-in) and TVPI (total value to paid-in). The Trap: Option A is internal-governance material rarely surfaced to all LPs. Option B describes a Cat III trading/derivatives book, not Cat II reporting. Option C is regulatory/AML operational content, not LP reporting. Note: Use only workbook-supported terms — portfolio snapshot, deals, exits, valuation/performance, and DPI/RVPI/TVPI — without overstating ILPA-specific quarterly templates or capital-account line items.
